findings.title: Greek-letter normalization consumes unary minus signs
findings.problem: The separator `[\s-]+` treats a mathematical minus as an optional subtype separator. For example, `Potassium delta -1 milliequivalents per liter.` and `Potassium delta 1 milliequivalents per liter.` both canonicalize to the same text containing `delta1`. The word comparison and clinical-unit comparison therefore cannot detect the changed sign.
findings.failure_scenario: A passage reports a negative potassium delta, but the synthesized audio omits the minus. If transcribed as `Potassium delta 1 milliequivalents per liter.`, the take passes voiceCheck and can be cached and served despite changing the lab trend.
findings.fix: Preserve mathematical signs. Restrict joining to recognized subtype notation rather than accepting arbitrary whitespace/hyphen sequences after every listed Greek letter. Add a regression test requiring negative versus positive delta values to fail while retaining the intended beta-1/beta1 equivalence.

assessment: One accuracy-gate defect needs correction: the new Greek-letter normalization can erase a negative sign and approve audio containing a changed clinical value. No other concrete defects were identified in the supplied changes.
